title: The city staffs itself: required everywhere before capacity anywhere, and a crew can be taken back

verified.the bug: game/sim/citizens/citizen_job_board.gd assign_jobs() walked job_ids filling each site `while site.assigned < site.capacity` and never read Site.required (line 35). At tick 24000 of first_night: 60 job slots, 39 required, 41 employable — every requirement fillable twice over — and 8 buildings on assigned:0 (5 of 7 coal generators, the granary, the survey hall, the only smelter). The Hearth held 8 against a need of 4.
verified.the fix: three passes: (1) every site's required crew in priority order off the idle queue; (2) anything still short is covered out of the SURPLUS of sites carrying more than they need, bounded at TRANSFERS_PER_PASS=2 and skipped entirely when nothing is short; (3) spare hands deepen crews toward capacity dealt out a LAYER at a time, so the Hearth cannot take every spare body for its fifth through eighth while the kitchen runs on the bare two that let it call itself staffed. Pass 2 exists because a two-pass hire alone changes nothing on a settled map: at t24000 every pair of hands was already employed, so nothing new can ever be crewed without a re-cut.
verified.iron_plate produced in 24000 ticks (seed: 0 -> 24  /  0 -> 29. The smelter had never completed a single craft; it ended the reference run reason='unstaffed', staffing 0.00, power 1.00.
verified.distinct items produced (seed 7): 7 -> 9 (iron_plate and slag: the smelting branch of the graph ran for the first time). iron_ore 14 -> 48, stone 28 -> 96, timber 44 -> 88, grain 60 -> 80. rations 558 -> 345 (the kitchen's surplus is spread across the city now).
verified.crafting graph depth: 2 -> 2, NOT past 2. Depth here = longest recipe chain reached; scrap->grain->ration was already 2 and scrap->iron_ore->iron_plate is also 2. Depth 3 needs gear/steel_plate/pipe_segment, which need a workshop or assembly_hall, and the first_night build AI places NEITHER in 24000 ticks (0 mentions in the log). Not a staffing problem — see 'open'.
verified.survey hall staffing: 0 of 3 -> 3 of 3 assigned, 2 present. research progress 0.752 in both runs, so the research crawl at 16/45 is gated on something other than the crew.
verified.tests/citizens/test_citizen_staffing.gd: TESTS PASSED against the new code; 4 of the 6 FAIL against the greedy loop restored into a scratch copy at /home/user/lcn-scratch (same 27 asserts execute in both trees, so nothing is skipped): 'and the site three places down the order still has its three' 1 vs >=3; 'the new building has the one person it needs' 0 vs 1; live world '4 building(s) short — smelter(9) has 0 of 3, workshop(8) has 1 of 4, survey_hall(10) has 0 of 3, granary(11) has 0 of 1 — while 8 worker(s) sit on crews that do not need them'; live world '25 employed for 19 required slots, and these have nobody at all: smelter(9), survey_hall(10), granary(11)'. The 2 that pass under both are the over-correction guards (a genuinely short city stays short; repeated passes settle instead of churning) and are meant to.
verified.the live tests are sized, not hoped: an earlier draft of the two live-world tests PASSED against the greedy loop, because the fixture city had labour to spare and greedy staffed everything by accident. The workshop row is now grown until its capacity covers every employable adult, and that precondition is asserted (assert_ge(_early_capacity, _workforce)) rather than assumed.
verified.tools/determinism.sh smoke determinism f: smoke IDENTICAL sha256 4f6962fd1f59c55a; determinism IDENTICAL sha256 f0a861053297fb62; script itself untouched
verified.hope / discontent at t24000: seed 7: 59.5 -> 38.4 hope, 78.1 -> 100.0 discontent, which looked like a serious regression until seed 11 was run BOTH ways: 58.75 -> 58.62 hope, 83.69 -> 83.97 discontent. The seed-7 swing is one extra old-age death at t18500 tipping a burial-law faction ultimatum that a headless harness has no player to answer; the underlying society inputs improved either way (warm_homes rate 0.88 -> 1.90, fed rate 0.51 -> 1.10, housed 13.0 -> 15.7).

open: [P11] / game/content/buildings/: the 6 'no crew' badges that survive are ALL buildings where staff_capacity is unset, so effective_staff_capacity() == workers_required and the crew has no depth: coal_generator, turret_mount, watchtower, granary, geothermal_tap, recuperator. One person assigned means zero present whenever that person is asleep, eating or walking — which is why 2-4 turrets read unmanned at nightfall in every screenshot. Setting staff_capacity = 2 on those .tres files is a one-line-per-file change in [P11]'s folder that my pass 3 will then use. I cannot make it; the folder is not mine.

[P11] / scenarios: the first_night build AI places no workshop and no assembly_hall in 24000 ticks, so gear, steel_plate, circuit and pipe_segment are unreachable and the crafting graph cannot go past depth 2 no matter how well staffed the city is. iron_plate now exists to feed one. This is the remaining half of the automation score.

[P04]: the smelter now runs but ends at reason='missing_input' with staffing 0.67 — it is starved of iron_ore, not of people. The ore_drill is at 3 of 6 and the only iron_ore source is the rubble_sorter. That is a logistics/recipe balance question, not a staffing one.

[P05] follow-up I did NOT take: staffing() is present/required, so a crew of exactly `required` reports below 1.0 most of the day. Pass 3 fixes this where capacity allows; where capacity == required (see the [P11] item above) it structurally cannot. If [P11] will not widen those defs, the alternative is for the board to target required x a duty-cycle factor, which changes what `required` means and should be a deliberate design call, not a matcher's private opinion.
perf: not measured. Four agents were on four cores throughout; the citizens perf suite passed but the numbers are meaningless. Only the integrator should grade perf.
